- If sentiment is negative over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — reduce forecast dip depth or add slight upward bias.
- If sentiment is positive and price has recently spiked, model often overshoots — cap forecast peak or add early correction downward.
- Model frequently overestimates short-term decline after recent highs — adjust downward bias for 3–5 day horizon.
- When sentiment is volatile or mixed, model tends to overfit recent noise — smooth forecast curve with weighted average of 3–5 prior values.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion toward prior 10-day average, model often ignores it — anchor forecast to 10-day moving average unless sentiment strongly contradicts.
- Model underestimates downward momentum when sentiment is negative — add 5–10% buffer below forecast for 10–15 day horizon.
- If sentiment is consistently negative and price is trending down, model often forecasts too slowly — accelerate downward slope by 1–2% per day.
- Model tends to overforecast upward moves when sentiment is positive — reduce forecast slope by 10–20% if sentiment is weak or fading.
